questions.question:
**Select the correct antonym of the given word.**

Exodus
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4 i.e. arrival**

**Exodus:** Refers to a mass departure of people.

**Arrival:** Refers to the coming of someone somewhere.

For e.g., My daughter promptly awaited the arrival of her father

Thus, it is clear that exodus and arrival are opposite words.

Let's look at the meaning of other words:

 
• **Exit:** Refers to the act of leaving from somewhere
 
• **Departure: **Refers to the act of leaving from somewhere, especially in order to reach somewhere else
 
• **Refund:** Refers to a certain amount being paid back to someone who has been wronged

Thus, options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

One of the boys from our school have been selected for National Badminton Championship
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**have been selected**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **'has been selected' **should be there in place of **'have been selected'**
 
• The **'one of'** is a **singular term** and generally used to talk about a noun or a pronoun.
 
• The** noun or a pronoun used after the phrase “one of”** is always in the **plural **form.
 
• The **helping verb will always be** in the **singular form**, as the helping verb agrees with “one of” and not with the plural noun in the sentence.

 **Example: ***One of the** students was** selected to visit NASA.*
 
• **Thus, the correct sentence is: ***One of the **boys** from our school **has** been selected for National Badminton Championship*

questions.question:
**​**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement. 

__The captain, as well as the players, was__ responsible for winning the trophy.

options.text: The captain as well as the players were
As The captain with the players were
The captain also the players were

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No improvement**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• ​When subjects are connected with **as well as, together with, along with, including, excluding, like, unlike, etc.**, the verb must agree with the first subject.

 **Example: **

 
 
• Maya as well as her friends is studying for the test.
 
 
 
• 
 **As well as** means **‘in addition to’**.

 
 
• 
 We can combine two sentences using as well as.

 Study the example given below.

 
 
• 
 Trees give us fruits. They also give us shade.
 
 
 
 
• 
 We can combine these two sentences using as well as.

 
 
• 
 Trees give us fruits as well as shade.
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
 In the given sentence, the first subject is 'the captain' which is singular, so a singular verb should be used.

questions.question:

Handle this glass table with care because it is ______.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4 i.e. fragile**

 
• The sentence refers to a glass table, meaning it is m**ade of glas**s.
 
• **Option **1 cannot be correct because 'ductile' refers to something that can be made into a thin wire which is not possible for glass
 
• **Option **2 cannot be the answer as 'volatile' refers to the quality of evaporating easily at lower temperatures, a quality that glass tables do not have
 
• **Option **3 cannot be the answer because 'frugal' refers to the human quality of being economical, something glass cannot do.

questions.question:
**​Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order**

A. However, they ignore the truth that progress and success are proportional to the labor they put in.

B. The general human tendency is to find faults in the policies framed by the government.

C. They blame the government for their slow progress, expecting miracles and magical transformation in their life.

D. So people openly criticize and condemn the policy makers.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1 i.e. BDCA**

The sentence begins with an introduction to the passage - B which talks about the general human tendency one has to find faults in government policies. Then comes sentence D which talks about how people who find fault condemn the policymakers. Then comes option C which talks about how the people find faults - blaming the government for their slow progress and how they expect miracles. The final sentence A talks about these people ignore the truth and the progress.

Thus, the correct answer is **option 1. **

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

I can swim very fast when I was only five.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __I can swim__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **'I could swim' **should be there in place of **'I can swim'**
 
• We use ***can*** and ***can't*** to talk about the ability to do something at a **specific time in the present or future.

 Example: ***I **can see** you.

 Help! I **can't breathe**.*
 
• 
 
We use ***could*** and ***couldn't*** to talk about the **past**:

 **Examples: ***She **could** **speak** several languages.

 They **couldn't** **dance** very well.*

 
 
• 
 
Since we are talking about past ability, we will use 'could'.

 

**Thus, the correct sentence is:***** **I **could** swim very fast when I was only five.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement. 

The Director will __agree with the proposal__ if we do not exceed the budget.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**agree to the proposal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agree to something: **to accept someone else’s plan, suggestion, etc

 **Example: **Often promoters will try to get people to agree to a deal.
 
• **Agree with** means to have the same opinion as another person or to approve of something.

 **Example: **I agree with you that spaghetti sauce can never have too much garlic.
 
• **Agree on** means to share the same opinion about items, topics, or standards

 **Example: **All parties agreed on plans to expand the Rideau Centre.
 
• The proposal is a kind of suggestion/ plan, **agree to **will be suitable

**Thus, the improved sentence is:** *The Director will **agree to the proposal__** if we do not exceed the budget.*

questions.question:
**Select the indirect narration of the given sentence.**

He said to the hotel receptionist, “Can you tell me the tariff of rooms?

options.text: He enquired the hotel receptionist if he can tell him the tariff of rooms.
He asked the hotel receptionist if he could tell him the tariff of rooms.
He asked the hotel receptionist that if he can tell him the tariff of rooms
He asked the hotel receptionist to tell him the tariff of rooms.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __He asked the hotel receptionist if he could tell him the tariff of rooms.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​We make changes in tenses of reported speech only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• When the reported speech is an interrogative sentence we follow these steps-
 
 
• Reporting verb 'said' is changed into 'asked'.
 
• connector 'if' or 'whether' is used in place of commas.
 
• Change the sentence, given in the reported speech__, from interrogative to assertive.
 
• Tense of reported speech is changed accordingly. ( in above sentence- 'can' changes into 'could')
 
• personal Pronouns of reported speech are changed as per subject and object of reporting verb. Here, the Second person- 'You' will change into 'he' as per object - 'me' (hidden).
 
 
 
• By following these steps we get the final sentence - *" He asked the hotel receptionist if he could tell him the tariff of rooms.**"*

Thus, the correct answer is **option 2.**

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

A. However, the rate of population increase is another important factor to consider.

B. This change can be expressed in two ways.

C. Growth of population refers to the change in the number of inhabitants of a country.

D. First, in terms of absolute numbers and second, in terms of percentage change.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1 i.e. CBDA**

The first statement, C introduces us to the topic at hand - the definition of growth, this is followed by statement B which explains the change that is referred to in statement C. Then comes statement D which then goes into deeper detail about the changes mentioned in the previous statements. Then comes the final statement, A which talks there is another factor that has to be taken into consideration.

Thus, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question:
**Select the passive form of the given sentence.**

The manager keeps the work pending.

options.text: The work are being kept pending by the manager.
The work was kept pending by the manager.
The work has been kept pending by the manager
The work is kept pending by the manager.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The work is kept pending by the manager.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The instructions given below should be followed while changing an assertive sentence to passive voice.

 
 
• Find the subject and object of the sentence and exchange their places; make changes in their cases.
 
• Use preposition by before the agent. (the manager)
 
• Use an appropriate helping verb in passive form according to the tense of the active form. (Present indefinite - is/am/are+ V3)
 
• Always use the third form of the main verb in passive form.
 
• At last line up the remaining part.
 
 

So, the final sentence is - *The work is kept pending by the manager.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• The voice of the sentence should be changed according to the following rules:

Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject
